answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money, one active association worker and three inactive workers. 2. Draw 8 Zoo cards and keep 4; discard the other 4. 3. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 4. All five Action cards begin side I; Animals goes in slot 1 and the other four are randomly placed in slots 2–5. 5. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, 1 for second, 2 for third and 3 for fourth; turn order is randomly chosen and proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C–G; Global setup, steps 6–7.

answers.answer: 1. In a two-player game, three left-column donation spaces are covered, and one level on each of the three face-up Base Conservation Project cards is covered: left level of the left card, middle level of the middle card and right level of the right card. Those spaces and levels are blocked to both players. 2. Three-player games use three face-up base projects; four-player games use four. The summary does not specify a different set of blocked spaces for three or four players. 3. Reveal the six-card display after everyone has selected their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Global setup 5b–5c and personal setup F–G.

answers.answer: 1. After using a card in slot 4, remove it, shift cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, and place the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before the action; each X-token spent then adds 1 strength, but X-tokens gained during that action cannot boost it. 3. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4. Complete the action and move the Action card before resolving effects that say ‘after finishing.’
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Taking a turn, X-tokens and ‘After finishing’ effects.

answers.answer: 1. You may not take a regular action that does nothing; for example, playing zero animals or building zero buildings is illegal. 2. Instead, choose an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token, unless you already hold 5. 3. Move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right as usual; the slot strength and upgrade side do not matter for this alternative action.
answers.evidence: Taking a turn; X-TOKEN action (alternative action).

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches its last space, ignore excess movement beyond that space. The player who reached it gains 1 X-token. 2. Finish the current turn; the break then occurs. 3. After the break, reset the token to its starting space and play continues clockwise with the next player. The summary does not describe a break cutting off the triggering player's remaining action.
answers.evidence: The Break track; Break trigger from effects.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then choose either a deck draw according to the side-I strength table (possibly requiring a discard) or, at strength 5+, snap exactly one card from anywhere in the display regardless of reputation and without drawing from the deck. 2. Cards II also advances 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or within reputation range in any order; its table gives 1/2/2/3/4 cards at strengths 1–5, with the indicated discard. Its snap option is available from strength 3 and still takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation. 3. The reputation restriction applies to the side-II draw option, not snapping. 4. Refill after the turn, not during it. There is no in-turn hand limit; check the hand limit only at breaks (3, or 5 with the hand-limit university).
answers.evidence: Cards action; Break procedure, step 1; Display timing.

answers.answer: 1. Reputation range includes the display folder matching your reputation space and all lower-numbered folders; the folder-to-space bands are 1: space 1, 2: spaces 2–3, 3: 4–6, 4: 7–9, 5: 10–12, and 6: 13–15. 2. Reaching reputation 10 or higher requires Cards II. 3. At space 15, each additional reputation step instead gives 1 appeal; reputation remains at 15. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation spaces and rewards; Reputation track and display.

answers.answer: 1. Build I constructs exactly one building, size no greater than strength; Build II constructs any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, and cannot build two identical buildings in the same action. 2. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placing each building. 3. Build adjacent to an existing building; the first building instead must touch at least one map-border space. 4. Do not overlap, go off-map, build on water/rock, or build on upgrade-restricted spaces without Build II. 5. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. A pavilion gives 1 appeal immediately once. Covered placement bonuses are taken immediately once; an empty standard enclosure does not give kiosk income, while occupied standard enclosures do.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: Side I, placement rules and Side II.

answers.answer: 1. Build I can build standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo per zoo. 2. Build II additionally permits Reptile Houses and Large Bird Aviaries; each zoo may have at most one Petting Zoo, one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary. 3. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter only through Sponsor cards. 4. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal; this can also be triggered by effects other than Build.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: Buildings available through Build; Side I/II.

answers.answer: 1. Benefits gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that same action. Pay for an item before receiving its own benefits, so money gained from playing an animal cannot pay that animal’s cost. 2. Immediate effects resolve as they occur; effects labeled ‘after finishing’ wait until the action is complete, including moving its Action card. 3. When effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Taking a turn: X-tokens; Animals action; Multiple simultaneous effects.

answers.answer: 1. Before playing an animal, meet all its left-side conditions and pay its cost; a matching-continent partner zoo reduces cost by 3 money per matching continent icon. Money effects from the play happen after paying. 2. Standard housing requires an empty standard enclosure at least the printed size; flip the entire enclosure to occupied, normally holding one animal. Petting Zoo animals must use a Petting Zoo. Reptiles and certain birds may instead use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if capacity allows; mark occupied spaces with supply player tokens and do not flip the special enclosure. 3. Meet water/rock adjacency requirements for whichever enclosure is chosen, counting distinct adjacent hexes. 4. Resolve each animal's immediate effects before playing the next animal; defer ‘after finishing’ effects until the Animals action and card movement are complete. Simultaneous effects may be ordered by the player.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action: Side I, enclosure state and special-enclosure capacity.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II may play animals from the display if they are within reputation range, in addition to animals from hand. Pay the display folder number as an extra cost; display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. 2. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the beginning of the action, so the increased range applies to animals played during it. 3. Animals II permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action: Side II.

answers.answer: 1. Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you relocate suitable existing animals into that new building, choosing separately for each animal, and only if capacity and terrain requirements are met. 2. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all its requirements, including terrain; if none does, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets its size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip none. 3. Add the animal's indicated number of supply player tokens to the new special enclosure. The summary describes no further eligibility count beyond all corresponding eligible animals that fit.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure.

answers.answer: 1. Association tasks have strengths: increase reputation 2, gain partner zoo 3, gain university 4, and conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task; Association II can perform one or more different tasks whose total strength value does not exceed the action's strength. 3. A task needs one active worker the first time before a break; if one of your workers is already on that task, place two workers to repeat it; if three are there, it cannot be performed again until after the break. 4. Other players' workers on the task do not matter.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: Side I, tasks and Side II.

answers.answer: 1. Partner zoos and universities are taken from available tiles on the Association board and placed on the lowest empty space in the corresponding column of your map; take any space bonus immediately. 2. Partner zoos must be from different continents, max 4; no duplicate university type. If every zoo available is one you already own, or placement is impossible, you cannot take a partner zoo. 3. University acquisition gives its printed reputation and research icons, plus any covered-space reward. 4. Partner zoos give their continent icon and reduce matching animal costs; universities give research icons and their stated benefits. The hand-limit university raises the limit from 3 to 5; other universities do not. 5. A third/fourth partner zoo requires upgraded Association. During a break, tiles are restocked except types already owned by every player, and duplicates are not added.
answers.evidence: Setup: University tiles; ASSOCIATION action: Gain partner zoo/university; Break procedure step 3.

answers.answer: 1. Conservation project work can support a project already in play or introduce a Conservation Project card and support it immediately. A new card normally comes from hand; Association II can use an in-range display card, paying its folder number, with no refill until turn end. 2. Choose a condition you fulfill and a reward level with no player's token; you may support a given project only once normally, even if another level is open. Put one token from the left edge of your map on the condition, then take the reward and uncover the map bonus immediately, before or after the project reward as chosen; recurring map bonuses also pay at each break. 3. New projects enter above the Association board; if they exceed the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to their owners' supplies while leaving map bonuses activated. 4. Base projects below the board never move or refill. The summary does not state a separate general supply quantity limit for project tokens.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: Conservation project work; Discarded conservation projects.

answers.answer: 1. A Release into the Wild project uses the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement, not its actual enclosure: size 1 or 2 qualifies for 2−, exactly size 3 for 3, and size 4 or 5 for 4+. Match the required animal category/icon. 2. Lose only that animal's printed appeal before gaining conservation; discard it and lose its icons, but keep its conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects. 3. If it could live in a special enclosure and its required special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you must remove those tokens; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone if none meets all, or none if none meets size. This frees a standard enclosure where one is flipped. 4. The summary does not specify any additional general reputation loss; it says playing a new release project grants 1 reputation, whereas supporting an existing one does not.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: Release into the wild projects.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand when strength is at least its level and all card conditions are met. Sponsors II may play multiple cards from hand and/or reputation-range display; strength +1 must be at least the sum of their levels, and display cards cost their folder number. Sponsors II also permits upgrade-conditioned cards. 2. Resolve each card's instant effects fully before playing the next; defer ‘after finishing’ effects until the action ends. 3. If only taking the break-track money option, Sponsors I advances the token by strength and gives that much money; Sponsors II advances it by strength and gives twice that amount. The full amount is gained even if fewer steps are needed to reach the end of the track.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action: Side I/II.

answers.answer: 1. At a break, in order: discard to hand limit; clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and restock partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset the Break token. 2. Hand limit is 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university. 3. A kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify. 4. When multiple players take display cards during break income, resolve affected players clockwise starting at the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), refilling the display after each player's income before the next chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation choose either an Action-card upgrade or activate another association worker. At 5 and 8 choose 5 money or one Bonus tile beside that space; tiles are removed after use, but the 5-money choice remains. At 10, the first player to reach or exceed it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. 2. Check the end trigger at the end of your own turn or during a break: if appeal and conservation are in the same scoring area or pass each other, the end begins. Appeal gained on another player's turn waits until your turn end or a break unless another trigger occurs first. The triggering player completes their turn; each other player gets one turn. If triggered during a break, every player gets one more turn. 3. If nobody reaches 10 conservation before the end, all players discard one Final Scoring card before scoring. Each Final Scoring card is capped at 4 conservation points. 4. Victory points equal appeal minus the lowest appeal value in the scoring area containing your conservation counter. Highest positive score wins; ties go to the player with more supported projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions; Final scoring.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the nine Bonus tiles and place one face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 and two beside 8; do not cover the two spaces with icons, and return the other five tiles to the box. 2. If a component supply runs out, use a suitable substitute; physical stock alone does not prevent a legal play. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Setup: Global setup step 2; Component supply.

answers.answer: 1. For advanced maps, either take two random maps and choose one, or lay out player count plus one advanced maps and choose one each in reverse turn order. Return unselected maps to the box. 2. Map A starts with an empty size-3 enclosure and a kiosk on its indicated spaces; the printed kiosk already counts as built. The summary does not give a fixed enclosure/kiosk for Map A beyond this setup, and does not describe Map A as an advanced map.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A.

answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 7 player tokens on the designated spaces at the left edge of their zoo map; the remainder stays beside the map. 2. Hire/activate reserve workers from the lowest remaining supply space upward. 3. Map A's third partner zoo grants a worker and its fourth grants 2 conservation; hiring the last worker can also trigger a map reward if printed. The summary does not enumerate which other maps grant a last-worker reward.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2–C3; Map A bonuses; Association worker supply.

answers.answer: 1. When you earn an Action-card upgrade, flip one card of your choice from side I to side II; it stays in its current slot. 2. Its improved action is usable from your next action; the current action keeps the strength and capabilities set at its start. 3. It counts immediately as upgraded for conditions. 4. The summary says there are four ways to upgrade and one lets you choose an alternative, so you cannot upgrade all five cards.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I draws/discards at strengths 1–5+: 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1. 2. A required discard may be either a card just drawn or one already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw tables.

answers.answer: 1. Animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. Bears remain a category even when shown with a herbivore or predator icon; Petting Zoo animal is a separate category. Count both special categories unless the effect explicitly excludes them.
answers.evidence: Animal categories (7); Base glossary: shared principles.

answers.answer: 1. Donation is available only with Association II, after performing at least one association task in that same action; it needs no worker and is limited to one donation per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible and cover that donation space with one of your supply tokens to gain 1 conservation. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. 3. After all spaces except the last are covered, each later donation costs 12 money and places no further token. 4. Donations do not require project conditions; the summary states the above requirements.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: Side II donation.

answers.answer: 1. Count upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards; also count water/rock requirements in the upper-left of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards. Count partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side conditions, conservation-project icons, a university's reputation award or hand-limit mark. 3. A card counts its own icons for its effects; doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules when they conflict.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo; shared principles.

answers.answer: 1. To satisfy two water or rock spaces, count two distinct adjacent map hexes of that terrain; multiple edges touching the same hex count only once. In a larger region, count only hexes actually adjacent to the enclosure. 2. Connected terrain regions do not make non-adjacent hexes count. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are not terrain spaces.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action: water and rock; Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes.

answers.answer: 1. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting a release project already in play does not grant that play bonus. 2. Breeding Program projects use the same requirement for all three reward spaces, so choose any available space. Normal support rules still require an unoccupied reward level and a project not already supported by you.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: Release into the wild; Icon-count projects.

answers.answer: 1. In an effect written X:Y, X is the condition and Y is the reward. 2. If X has no number or says ‘per,’ each fulfillment pays once. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; when several thresholds are listed, use the highest threshold met.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: shared principles, X:Y effects.

answers.answer: 1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes those for every player.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: shared principles.

answers.answer: 1. Unique buildings enter play only through their Sponsor cards and must be placed when the Sponsor is played; if no legal placement is possible, you cannot play the card. 2. Use the matching tile with its colored face up; rotate freely but do not flip it. Apply normal placement and printed terrain adjacency rules. No size-based building payment is due. 3. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals and never count as water or rock spaces. 4. The summary does not state a general option to play the Sponsor while leaving its unique building unplaced; placement is required.
answers.evidence: Unique buildings; Sponsor card layout.

answers.answer: 1. After finishing the Animals action and moving its card, perform the granted Action or Determination. Use that Action card normally and move it to slot 1 afterward. 2. A named Action, such as Sponsors, cannot be replaced by taking an X-token. Determination (Any Action) may choose any action, including the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Action / Determination.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion and Dominance take project cards from the unused face-down base-project deck: Assertion chooses a project; Dominance searches for its named project. 2. Dominance has no effect if the named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediate support the obtained card through Association, placing it above the board; it does not join the base-project row below the board.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion / Dominance.

answers.answer: 1. Boost and Clever resolve after finishing Animals and moving the Animals card. 2. Clever puts the chosen Action card in slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. Boost puts its named card in slot 1 or 5; moving to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left. 3. The summary does not specify other slot choices for these effects.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Boost / Clever.

answers.answer: 1. Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Constriction all use an eligibility floor of at least 5 appeal for affected zoos. 2. Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal; Constriction affects every other eligible zoo ahead on appeal and/or conservation. Hypnosis targets the highest-appeal eligible zoo; Pilfering 1 targets highest appeal and Pilfering 2 separately targets highest appeal and most conservation, with a conservation target needing at least 1 conservation. 3. Ties are chosen by the acting player where specified; self-targeting Hypnosis or Pilfering has no effect. The playing animal's new appeal normally need not count when choosing targets because its appeal can be gained before or after the ability. 4. If the group prefers, use the card's solo-marked alternative text instead of interactive abilities; this does not require solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities; Interactive target reference.

answers.answer: 1. Constriction affects every other zoo with at least 5 appeal that is ahead of you on appeal and/or conservation. Ahead on one track gets 1 token; ahead on both gets 2. 2. Put tokens on the target's highest slots: slot 5 for one, slots 4 and 5 for two. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Each marked action loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. At effective strength zero or below, boost to at least one, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. 4. Return the token after acting with the card, or without effect at the break.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference; Constriction.

answers.answer: 1. If Constriction reduces an action's effective strength to zero or below, the card cannot perform that regular action at that strength; use enough X-tokens to reach at least one, take the alternative X-token action, or wait until it is at least in slot 3. 2. The alternative X-token action may be used only if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens; using the marked card removes its Constriction token. The summary does not say the zero-strength card can simply be used as a regular action.
answers.evidence: Constriction; X-TOKEN action.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 gives up to two selections; after each card, decide again which option to use: discard a display card, or discard a hand card then draw one deck card. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replaced immediately: shift higher folders down and draw into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Digging 2.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal need not occupy a new enclosure if your zoo already has a herbivore requiring at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 3. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot share that enclosure. 4. Releasing a flock animal still frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure even if it originally shared; the game does not track which animal originally occupied which enclosure.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Flock Animal.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker, moving it to your notepad for immediate use. 2. Take a last-worker map reward if one is shown. 3. If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Full-throated; Association worker supply.

answers.answer: 1. Hunter X reveals X cards from the deck, adds one revealed Animal card to your hand and discards the other revealed cards. 2. If no revealed card is an Animal, discard all revealed cards and add none to hand.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Hunter X.

answers.answer: 1. Hypnosis selects among tied players with the highest appeal who have at least 5 appeal; if you are the target, it has no effect. 2. Copy only an Action card in the target's slot 1, 2 or 3. Use that card's owner's upgraded/unupgraded side; your own X-tokens may be spent. 3. Venom and Constriction on the targeted card apply and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally. 4. The summary does not specify a general rule that copied-card tokens move with the card; it explicitly states Venom and Constriction are discarded afterward and Multiplier cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference: Hypnosis.

answers.answer: 1. Put a gained Multiplier immediately on the named Action card; a bonus-tile Multiplier can go on any card, including Animals. 2. On its next use, you may execute that action twice in succession at the same base strength; move the Action card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Additional Multiplier tokens add one execution apiece, so two tokens allow up to three actions. 3. Resolve each regular execution with its permitted choices; do not mix one regular action and one X-token alternative. A multiplied X-token alternative can take two X-tokens, subject to the 5-token maximum. 4. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions are done. A break triggered in the first execution waits until the whole turn is finished. Return used tokens to supply; unused tokens are removed at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens on one Action card permit up to three executions on its next use. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to your five-token limit, but cannot mix an X-token action with a regular action.
answers.evidence: Multiplier: Additional Multipliers; Choices.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking permits placing the Large Bird Aviary before Build is upgraded, provided your zoo does not already have one and a legal site exists. 2. Other placement restrictions still apply, including Build II for upgrade-marked map spaces. 3. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Posturing; Peacocking.

answers.answer: 1. Petting Zoo animals give appeal in order: first 3, second 6, third 9. 2. The one Petting Zoo holds at most three such animals. 3. They count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Petting Zoo animal; Base Sponsor reference.

answers.answer: 1. Pilfering 1 targets the highest-appeal eligible zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal zoo and the most-conservation zoo. Targets must each have at least 5 appeal; the conservation leader must have at least 1 conservation. 2. The acting player chooses among ties. If the acting player is the target, that part has no effect. If everyone has zero conservation, Pilfering 2's conservation-target part has no effect, but its appeal-target part still resolves normally.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference; Pilfering X.

answers.answer: 1. The affected player chooses to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. With no hand cards, give 5 money; with less than 5 money, give a card. If there is neither a hand card nor 5 money, give all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated Pilfering sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch tucks up to X hand cards beneath the animal for 2 appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard those tucked cards, but keep the appeal already gained. 2. Sunbathing sells up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Scavenging; Pouch X.

answers.answer: 1. Resistance means an extra Final Scoring card drawn before the 10-conservation milestone joins the cards from which you discard one when the milestone occurs. 2. At game end, score every Final Scoring card you still hold; each card has its own cap of 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Resistance.

answers.answer: 1. Scavenging shuffles the discard pile face down, draws randomly from it, makes the card's stated selection and then returns the discard pile face up. 2. For Scavenging 3, draw 3 random cards, keep 1 and discard the others.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Scavenging.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one card from the display regardless of reputation; it does not allow a deck draw as an alternative. Refill at the ordinary end-of-turn timing. 2. Sponsor Magnet takes display Sponsors regardless of reputation; if there is no Sponsor in the display, it has no effect. Refill at the end of the turn.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Snapping; Sponsor Magnet.

answers.answer: 1. Venom X places X tokens on every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal, on that zoo's lowest slots (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicate tokens return to supply. 2. Using a card with Venom removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including when using the X-token alternative if you have fewer than 5 X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one remains; if unable, undo the turn and choose another action. You cannot avoid payment by spending all money. 4. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom X.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian immediately gives 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities. 2. It reduces the required strength for conservation project work from 5 to 4. 3. Its final-scoring reward is 1 conservation for three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 203 Veterinarian.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough's immediate appeal is 2 per previously supported project, counted by player tokens missing from the left edge of your zoo map. 2. At each break it gives 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 206 Medical Breakthrough.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research gives 1 conservation per two different continent or animal-category icons in your zoo; research icons do not count. A card counts its own matching icons for its own effect, and doubled icons count twice. 2. Each other player gets 2 money for each conservation point you gain.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 207 Basic Research.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon immediately. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final condition gives 1 conservation if you have five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 208 Science Library.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon immediately. 2. Each Americas icon played lets you build one free kiosk, subject to normal placement and kiosk spacing. 3. Its final condition gives 1 conservation with at least five kiosks.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 210 Expert on the Americas.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon immediately. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card beneath it for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 212 Expert on Australia.

answers.answer: 1. Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program each get two supply tokens when played. When supporting a base project that remains below the Association board, you may return exactly one token as any one icon; never use both tokens for a single support. A base-origin project card later played above the board does not qualify. 2. Each card's final condition gives 1 conservation after five or more project supports, counted by tokens missing from your map's left edge.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 215 Global Breeding Program; 218 Breeding Program.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer lets each Build action add one extra copy of a building built in that same action without extra strength. Only one extra building may be added, even if several different buildings were built; pay its normal cost and follow placement rules. Special enclosures retain their one-per-type limit. 2. Its final reward is 5 appeal with the map fully covered except water and rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 217 Engineer.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2. It lets you cover water and rock spaces and ignore animal and unique-building terrain requirements; printed terrain icons still count. Terrain need not be covered to satisfy full-map coverage. 3. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo. 4. Its final reward is 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 219 Diversity Researcher.

answers.answer: 1. Archaeologist triggers whenever you receive an actual placement bonus on a border space. 2. For each such bonus, choose any uncovered placement bonus on your map as an additional bonus; copied bonuses may be the same or different, and resolve them in your chosen order. 3. Its final condition gives 1 conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water and rock. 4. The Hollywood Hills H spaces are not placement bonuses and do not trigger it.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 221 Archaeologist; Map 8 Hollywood Hills.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. You may support the same release project repeatedly using different qualifying animals, but may put at most one token on that project per Association action. 3. Each token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 224 Migration Recording.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and select the next qualifying player. 3. Its final condition gives 1 conservation if you have all five continent icons.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 225 Quarantine Lab.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Special Assignment permanently chooses small or large; mark that choice with a supply token. Reveal deck cards until finding an animal of the chosen size class, keep it and discard the others. Small means printed standard size 1 or 2, including Petting Zoo animals; large means size 4 or 5. 2. Thereafter, chosen small animals gain 2 extra appeal or chosen large animals gain 4; you cannot play the opposite type. Size-3 animals remain legal but receive no bonus.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 227 WAZA Special Assignment.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal immediately. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals may play one additional small animal from hand under normal costs/rules, then take one small animal from the display into hand regardless of reputation. You may take the display animal even if you decline the extra play. 3. If the original Animals action mixes small and large animals, the extra effect does not apply.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 228 WAZA Small Animals Program.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon immediately. 2. Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, even several spaces in one building; a space touching multiple water hexes pays only once. 3. Its final condition gives 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected, with none isolated.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 241 Hydrologist.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut is a unique building placed through its Sponsor card. 2. Whenever you play a bird icon, draw two cards from the deck, keep one and discard the other.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 249 Barred Owl Hut.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank is a unique building that must be placed adjacent to water. 2. Whenever you play a reptile icon, you may sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard the sold cards.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 250 Sea Turtle Tank.

answers.answer: 1. For each predator icon played, Spotted Hyena Compound triggers Hunter, revealing a number of cards equal to your total predator icons. 2. If one new card has two predator icons, resolve two Hunters sequentially, counting both new icons each time.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 252 Spotted Hyena Compound.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable enters with three supply tokens. Per herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a Sponsor in your hand's level to play that Sponsor, subject to its normal conditions. 2. The Stable's own herbivore icon can trigger this when it is played, and it allows three uses total. 3. The card source is hand; the summary does not allow using the display for this ability.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 253 Okapi Stable.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School immediately grants 1 reputation and 1 conservation. 2. Place its unique building covering at least two border spaces. 3. Take one card from within reputation range in the display or draw one from the deck. Resolve simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 254 Zoo School.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance is a unique building placed on two border spaces; unlike ordinary buildings it need not touch an existing building. Other placement rules still apply, and later buildings may attach to it. 2. At breaks it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may stand beside a kiosk. 3. It counts as a unique building for adjacent kiosk income. 4. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map excluding water and rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 257 Side Entrance.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals immediately gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock spaces never count. 2. At game end, gain 1 conservation per group of six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately (the example groups of 13, 6, 3 and 2 yield 3 points). 3. Upgrade-restricted spaces count even if Build was not upgraded. Terrain spaces do not count.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 260 Native Farm Animals.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer immediately gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon; research icons do not count. 2. Each newly introduced category or continent later gives 1 appeal and 2 money. 3. A new card with two copies of the same new icon grants the novelty benefit only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 262 Explorer.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place one size-5 standard enclosure for free under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition, such as one required icon or the Animals upgrade; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference: 263 WAZA Large Animal Program; Map 6 Research Institute.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo gives 1 conservation for each animal category in which your zoo has more icons than the player to your right, up to 4 conservation. 2. If that player has none of a category, one of your icons is enough to exceed them. The summary does not give additional special handling for ties beyond requiring strictly more icons.
answers.evidence: Base Final Scoring and map clarifications: Biodiverse Zoo.

answers.answer: 1. Map 1 Observation Tower grants its 2-appeal bonus to an animal housed in a standard enclosure adjacent to the tower hex itself; adjacency to another rock hex is insufficient. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. Housing an animal there grants the two appeal again even if a previous animal was released. 4. The Tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1, Observation Tower.

answers.answer: 1. Map 2 Outdoor Areas qualifies a standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex itself, not merely another water hex. 2. That enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; this cannot be ignored for release or transfer (a physical size-2 enclosure there counts as size 4). 3. It does not affect special enclosures and is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2, Outdoor Areas.

answers.answer: 1. Map 4 Commercial Harbor activates when a building is placed on its adjacent building space; your first building may start beside it but need not. 2. Its discard ability may be used before, during or after your action, once per own turn, never during a break or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor itself is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4, Commercial Harbor.

answers.answer: 1. Map 5 Park Restaurant gives break income of 1 money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type, occupancy, or whether multiple hexes belong to one building. Empty enclosures qualify. 2. Restaurant is not a building and does not count as a kiosk neighbor. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus allows one Reptile House or one Large Bird Aviary free, even before Build II, but not both; other normal placement rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Map 5, Park Restaurant.

answers.answer: 1. On Map 8 Hollywood Hills, cover H spaces by placing buildings under ordinary placement rules. When an H is covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears, keep it and discard the others. 2. H spaces are not placement bonuses and do not trigger Archaeologist. 3. Once all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. The third/fourth bonus partner zoos still require Association II, and bonus buildings still require Build II to cover upgrade-marked spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8, Hollywood Hills.

answers.answer: 1. To use the pay-money-to-play-a-Sponsor bonus, pay money equal to that Sponsor's level and meet its normal play conditions. 2. Play the Sponsor only from hand, even if Sponsors II is upgraded; the display is not allowed for this bonus. 3. This bonus does not move the Sponsors Action card from its current slot.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: Bonus icons.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; gains beyond either track end are lost. 2. Reputation has a separate overflow: beyond space 15, each remaining reputation step becomes 1 appeal.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: Appeal cannot exceed 113, nor conservation 41; Reputation track and display.

answers.answer: 1. Venom targets every other zoo with higher appeal and at least 5 appeal. Hypnosis targets the highest-appeal zoo with at least 5, choosing among ties; it has no effect if that is you, and only slots 1–3 may be copied. 2. Pilfering 1 targets the highest-appeal eligible zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal and most-conservation eligible zoos, with the conservation leader requiring at least 1 conservation. Choose ties; self-targets have no effect. 3. Constriction targets each other eligible zoo ahead on appeal and/or conservation: one token if ahead on one track, two if ahead on both, placed in slots 5 and, for two tokens, 4.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference; Hypnosis; Pilfering X; Constriction.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal-card partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from that animal's continent; a Sponsor-card partner-zoo condition permits a partner zoo from any continent. 2. A red maximum-25-appeal condition allows play only while appeal is at most 25; the marker at 25 is only a reminder, not a general track cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed value. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one left-side card condition, but not terrain requirements.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: Bonus icons and condition clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine's Digging 2 offers two options for each selection: discard a display card (which is immediately replaced) or discard a hand card and draw one card from the deck. 2. It provides up to two selections, and the choice may change after each card.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Digging 2.

answers.answer: 1. When replenishing after taking display cards, move higher-folder cards down while preserving their order, then fill the empty folders from the deck. 2. The summary does not specify a different ordering rule for filling multiple empty folders. During a break, first discard folders 1–2, compact the remaining cards in order, then fill the vacancies from the deck.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display; Break procedure step 4.

answers.answer: 1. Build a standard enclosure with its empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. Gain each placement bonus on a space it covers immediately, once; later turning the enclosure to its occupied side does not award that bonus again.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: opening paragraph; placement rules.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches or exceeds 10 conservation, all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile. 2. The summary does not specify an orientation for that discarded card beyond face down.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: 10 conservation points.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; play proceeds clockwise. 2. There are no formal rounds: players take turns one at a time. 3. On a turn, take one regular action using one of the five Action cards; resolve its action and any applicable additional effects or bonuses according to their timing. The summary describes one regular action per turn, with card-triggered actions as extra effects.
answers.evidence: Setup: Global setup step 7; Overview; Turn Structure.

answers.answer: 1. If no player reaches 10 conservation before the game ends, every player must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins. 2. The summary does not further specify the exact timing beyond ‘before end-game scoring.’
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: 10 conservation points.
